A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Counting Stacked Objects and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original experiments on synthetic and real scenes, occupancy estimation, ablations and a counting study involving 33 human participants.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and supplementary Section 8 adds baseline evaluation against manually annotated visible-object counts.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same occupancy and thickness networks, objectives, segmentation, depth estimation and voxel-carving procedure. Removing an implementation-library sentence does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 adds visible-object-only counting as a baseline evaluation target on existing real scenes, extending evaluation beyond total stack counts. The underlying synthetic and real scene coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their comparator sets. New Table 6 reuses BMNet+ and SAM+CLIP for visibility-based evaluation and repeats the proposed method's total-count results; no baseline is added or replaced.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 8 introduces scoring against manually annotated visible counts using NAE, SRE and sMAPE. Existing experimental splits, model settings and total-count evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 8 and Table 6 examine whether the two 2D baselines still struggle when evaluated only on visible objects, accompanied by annotation examples in Figure 11. Existing depth/RGB ablations, complexity analysis and border-effects analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run confidence intervals, seed variability or significance tests. Existing human-study aggregation and distribution summaries are unchanged, and Table 6 follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds visible-only results: BMNet+ has NAE/SRE/sMAPE of 0.51/0.65/51.28, and SAM+CLIP has 0.57/0.81/50.84. Its all-object rows repeat Table 2, and Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. The new scores use different count targets and therefore do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1, formal occupancy-ratio definition, assumptions and other mathematical expressions are unchanged. The introduction's correction from number density to occupied-space fraction aligns its wording with the definition already present in v2.

C1.justification: The method's novelty, volume/occupancy decomposition, dataset and human-study contributions, and principal performance claims are retained. The abstract's added mention of manually verified counts already appeared in v2's introduction.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the visible-only evaluation: excluding hidden targets reduces baseline errors, while separating similar clumped visible objects remains difficult. This refines the explanation of baseline failures; existing method limitations and border-effects interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project link for code and datasets and states that released data include visible-object locations and counts. It removes v2's trimesh/alphashape implementation sentence. Other architecture, pretrained-model, hardware and runtime disclosures are retained; linked-resource availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 39 references and related-work positioning are retained. The new appendix repeats the existing distinction between visible-object counting methods and the proposed total-stack counting task.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the abstract, correct occupancy-ratio terminology, add acknowledgements and introduce one supplementary section with consequent renumbering. The main narrative and existing supplementary explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 11 with two visibility-annotation examples and Table 6 with visible-only and all-object blocks. The existing dataset-statistics figure becomes Figure 12 without changed content, while references and supplementary text undergo localized layout reflow.

improvement.justification: New Section 8 and Table 6 improve the context for v2's baseline comparisons by distinguishing visible-only from total-count evaluation. Corrected occupancy terminology and added code/data access information also improve clarity and potential reuse. These are limited gains: the core evidence is unchanged, the new analysis lacks a visible-only result for 3DC, and a brief implementation-library disclosure is removed.
